method: Rodríguez-Ridao 2020 read in full text on PMC (PMC7579505); Schoenfeld 2017 title confirmed by search; Schoenfeld 2016, ACSM 2009 and Helms 2016 from their published records (seed sources in content/plan.json). claims.claim: In a 2020 Spanish EMG study of the bench press at five inclinations, a 30 degree incline gave the highest upper (clavicular) pectoralis activity, and steeper inclines shifted work to the anterior deltoid.
claims.source_title: Effect of Five Bench Inclinations on the Electromyographic Activity of the Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoid, and Triceps Brachii during the Bench Press Exercise
claims.authors: Rodríguez-Ridao D, Antequera-Vique JA, Martín-Fuentes I, Muyor JM
claims.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(19):7339
claims.study_type: Cross-sectional EMG study: 30 resistance-trained adults (University of Almería), free-weight barbell bench press at 0, 15, 30, 45 and 60 degrees, 60% 1RM, 8 reps
claims.finding: Upper pectoralis %MVIC highest at 30 degrees (about 30%), lower at 60 degrees; middle and lower pectoralis fell as incline rose; anterior deltoid rose with incline, highest at 60 degrees. Measured muscle activity, not growth; free-weight bench, not a machine.
claims.on_screen: «على البنش» and «نشاط» in the narration; the caption says it measured activity, not growth.

claims.claim: Beginners: 3 sets of 8-12 repetitions; increase the load by about 2-10% when the top of the range is exceeded.
claims.source_title: Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
claims.finding: Novice: 1-3 sets of 8-12 repetitions; 2-10% load increase when 1-2 reps over the target can be done on two consecutive sessions.

claims.claim: Rest about 90-120 s between sets: rest longer than 60 s gave a small hypertrophy benefit, with no clear difference beyond about 90 s.
claims.source_title: Give it a rest: a systematic review with Bayesian meta-analysis on the effect of inter-set rest interval duration on muscle hypertrophy
claims.authors: Singer A, Wolf M, Generoso L, et al., Schoenfeld BJ
claims.finding: Small hypertrophic benefit for inter-set rest >60 s; no appreciable difference beyond 90 s (abstract read on frontiersin.org).

claims.claim: Pick a load that leaves about 2-3 repetitions in reserve (practical guidance, caption only).
claims.source_title: Application of the Repetitions in Reserve-Based Rating of Perceived Exertion Scale for Resistance Training
claims.authors: Helms ER, Cronin J, Storey A, Zourdos MC
claims.finding: RIR-based scale for choosing and adjusting load.
